title: Streamline Ribbons: Per-Model & Per-Route Performance Dashboard + Chart Spec
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design spec and prototype for a compact, scannable per-model and per-route performance dashboard called 'Streamline Ribbons'. Focus is latency (P50/P95/P99), throughput (RPS / tokens/sec), token metrics (tokens/request, input/output tokens), cost breakdown and cache-hit signals. This ticket covers layout, visual encodings, chart interactions, accessibility considerations, and handoff artifacts for engineering and product reviews.
background: Product asked for a lightweight dashboard to help platform engineers and product owners quickly assess model health per route and compare model variants during rollouts. Existing performance canvases are comprehensive but dense; this design prioritizes quick triage, cost attribution, and easy drilldowns into token-level anomalies.
goals: Provide one-line health indicators for each model-route pair
Surface P95/P99 latency regressions with contextual cost impact
Enable fast comparison between model versions across a selected time window
Support drilldown into token-level waterfall traces and batch-size distributions
Be usable inside small panes (dashboard cards) and expanded modal views
non_goals: Replacing the full Performance Studio UX
Deep APM-style trace capture — engineering will link to existing trace view
Realtime streaming visualizations for every metric at sub-second intervals
audience: Platform engineers, ML engineers, SREs, Product managers responsible for model SLAs
chart_specs: Header strip: model name, route id, latest deployment tag, small health chip (green/amber/red) computed from weighted score of error-rate, P95 latency, and cache-hit drop

Sparkline row: compact 180px-wide sparkline showing selected metric (toggle: latency/throughput/cost). Sparkline uses 1m sampling for last 24h by default; hover shows exact aggregated datapoints and event markers (deployments, incidents)

Latency mini-heat: 3-band heat row visualizing P50/P95/P99 as stacked color bands. Color ramp: neutral blue for baseline P50, amber for P95 crossing SLA, red overlay for P99 spikes. Y-axis collapsed; tooltip shows numeric ms values and sample size

Throughput area: small stacked area card showing RPS and tokens/sec. Two series: requests/sec (solid) and tokens/sec (dashed overlay). Use shared time axis; y-axis auto-scales but shows toggle for logarithmic scale for heavy-tailed workloads

Token distribution violin: compact violin plot representing tokens/request distribution over the selected window. Includes median line and 10/90 percentile markers. Helps diagnose long-tail prompts driving token cost

Batch-size histogram: micro histogram of batch sizes observed by runtime in same window. X-axis integer batch size, Y-axis frequency. Bars colored by whether batched requests met latency SLO (green) or not (red)
Waterfall mini-link: lightweight waterfall thumbnail representing average token-latency slices (token decode time vs attention time). Clicking opens full token waterfall trace in Trace Viewer
Cost bar: micro stacked bar with cost breakdown: model compute, I/O, caching savings. Show cost per 1k requests and cost delta vs previous period
SLA ribbon: thin horizontal ribbon across card that overlays SLA thresholds and recent alert markers. Hover reveals alert summary and link to incident timeline
Compare toggle: allows selecting up to 3 model versions or routes. When active, the card switches to comparison mode and shows side-by-side sparklines and a delta summary row with direction chevrons

Drilldown behavior: clicking the card opens a modal with expanded charts (time ranges up to 90 days), top contributing prompts, example traces, and quick actions (pin route, create alert, start rollout rollback)

Sampling and aggregation: default aggregation window 1 minute for last 24h, 5 minutes for 7d, 30 minutes for 90d. Use weighted percentile aggregation where appropriate. Include 'raw samples' toggle for high-fidelity debugging
Missing data: show dotted-line interpolation and distinct empty-state pattern along timeline. Provide 'data stale since' message if no data for > 15m

Color palette and semantics: primary metric color = Redwood Teal for baseline, Accent Amber for warning band, Accent Red for critical. Use gray scale for secondary axes and context lines. Maintain WCAG contrast ratio >= 4.5 for text and critical markers

Annotations and events: deploy markers (triangle), CI/CD rollouts (square), manual rollback (diamond), incident start (exclamation). Event tooltips contain timestamp, author, and link to PR or incident doc
Accessibility: all micro-charts must expose textual summaries via aria-labels and have keyboard focus states. Provide CSV export of the card's underlying aggregated series
Performance budget: each card should render under 150ms on average on console view; engineering to implement progressive hydration and skeleton placeholders
layout_and_responsiveness: Card sizes: Compact (240x120), Regular (480x160), Expanded modal full width
Grid: 12-column responsive grid in console. Cards span 3 columns (compact), 6 columns (regular), 12 columns (expanded)
Collapse rules: in narrow viewcards collapse violin and histogram into an accordion; keep health chip, sparkline and cost bar visible
Print/export: cards should render to PNG with high-DPI export option for reporting
interactions: Hover: show tooltip with metric values, window aggregation, and sample count
Click: opens modal with detailed analytics and actionable links
Compare: multi-select checkboxes at card level to enable side-by-side comparison
Pin: top-right pin toggles to keep route in a user's quick-access list
Context menu: right-click exposes 'Open in Performance Studio', 'Create alert', 'Copy route id', 'View logs'
acceptance_criteria: Design assets: Figma file with Compact/Regular/Expanded variants and component tokens provided
Engineering Handoff: chart spec doc with series names, units, aggregation rules, sampling windows and API field names
Accessibility checklist: aria labels, keyboard interactions, color contrast passed
Performance: prototype renders under target budget on a representative dataset
Review approvals: PM, Eng lead for runtime telemetry, Security sign-off if needed
engineering_handoff_notes: Primary telemetry fields expected from telemetry API: ts, model_id, route_id, version, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, rps, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, cache_hit_rate, error_rate, cost_compute_usd
Aggregation: percentiles are pre-aggregated in telemetry pipeline. For violin and histograms, telemetry will provide distribution buckets or raw sample digests
Event types: deploy_event, incident_event, rollout_event with metadata (author, link, message)
UI-level smoothing: 5-point exponential smoothing optional; default off for comparisons
review_comments: PM (Lydia Park): Good lightweight tradeoffs. Add a quick 'cost impact' callout when P95 increases >20%
Eng (Samir Patel): Need clarity on percentile computation and whether p99 is computed from samples or from digest. Also confirm batch-size histogram bucket boundaries
SRE (Monique Li): Suggest including a synthetic request success-rate micro metric for quick health checks
Design (Ava Chen): Updated color ramps to pass WCAG and adjusted violin baseline so median line is 2px to be visible at small sizes
Accessibility lead (Diego Ramos): Confirmed keyboard tab order and aria-label content for sparklines; requested text alternatives for all event markers
risks_and_open_questions: Telemetry ingest: p99 accuracy depends on upstream digest; worst-case p99 may be approximate
Card density: squeezes many visualizations into small cards; risk of overwhelming new users — need telemetry for feature usage to iterate
Delta computations: how to surface statistically significant change vs noise? PM asks for hysteresis rules for alert coloring
Cross-region comparisons: are timezones normalized at ingestion? Need to document timezone handling
